literature_proposed.summary: No proof of this statement is known, and none is expected from the literature as it stands. The statement implies the irrationality of sum_{n>=2} 1/(n!-1) (Erdős problem 68, open since 1968) through the elementary steps erdos-68--h1 and erdos-68--h2, and it is strictly stronger than that irrationality: it asks that the fractional part of F_N = sum_{n=2}^N N!/(n!-1) leave the window [1-2/N, 1) for infinitely many N, while irrationality only excludes one point of that window for each N. Equivalently, the fractional part of sum_{n=2}^N (N! mod (n!-1))/(n!-1), a statement about the residues of N! modulo the numbers n!-1. No result on the distribution of these residues, or of the fractional parts of such sums, is known to us.
